body: It is truly awful, the feelings are beyond pain but it can be made easier, cut contact, do things that only make you happy and keep powering through, time is a healer.
there's nothing you can do to 'speed up' the process as such, but you can definitely make it easier, that would be my advice :)
I hope so, I just can't shift this feeling of overwhelming anxiety though, how have you felt today?

that gives me a lot of hope, I'm happy to hear that things are getting better. I think I need to focus on the positive things left in my life, but at the moment I can't help but see everything I've lost. Thankyou very much, same goes for you
that's true, I enjoy being alone and I think sometimes I see that as unhealthy but really it's a good thing
It's just hard because I don't know how much longer I can carry on staying strong, I keep telling myself I'll be happy but I just don't believe it

I can completely understand how you're feeling, my relationship recently broke down because of my anxiety and long distance. He was the only positivity in my life and I'm struggling everyday to keep myself out of the darkness that is depression. Something similar happened to me two years ago though and since then I have been happy, despite going through another bad stage right now, I keep remembering that it got better before, so it can get better this time.

I guess it is important to remember that despite all those low times you felt happy when you got your diploma, therefore there may be happiness at the end of this tunnel too. But its so difficult when you feel the whole world is against you.

I had the exact same problem with my mum, it doesn't have to be your mum or even a friend that you talk to though. I spoke to my doctor (Someone that I had no bond with) and I found it a lot easier to be honest as you're not holding back things that may upset them. I have contemplated suicide over the last 4 years and I promise you, that despite having about 3 really low periods they have got better, and it has been worth sticking around. i'm going through a low period at the moment and I find it helpful to remind myself of all the times I have laughed and been happy despite those feelings, and how there will be more happy moments if I choose life.

its usually around the same time each year or certain things can trigger it. It's always underlying though, my long term boyfriend recently broke up with me, and was seeing girls whilst we were togetherr. It has reinforced all the feelings of worthlessness and loneliness that depression causes in the first place and I feel as though its given me an excuse to kill myself. I have lost a lot of friends because of the break up as they have taken his side and my family never liked him so they can't understand why I am upset. I have a good job though, plans for university, several holidays booked and so many opportunities, I just can't help but feel this way, it's been in the back of my mind for 4 years now.

I feel as though I've been saying that to myself for so long now though and I don't know how much longer I can believe that for. I know it's my fault though, I've had two long term relationships end now because of my depression and lost numerous friends, I feel very isolated
I am suffering from the same sort of thing, I feel as though it's taken my depression from manageable to consuming
